pr_title: Copy I18N assemblies when running without the linker
pr_comments: I'm not sure what our tolerance is for taking build changes at this point. IMO, this should be a low risk change even for RC. It cleans up a property name (which is a bit optional) and copies additional assemblies to the output folder. I kept the implementation intentionally simple to avoid complicating our MSBuild targets.

issue_context.title: Is setting BlazorWebAssemblyEnableLinking to 'true' required?
issue_context.body:
[EDIT by @guardrex to fix the character encoding]

Is it possible that `<MonoLinkerI18NAssemblies>all</MonoLinkerI18NAssemblies>` is not taking into account when the linker is disabled? For development builds this seems to be the default since 3.2.0 Preview 2.

This is working for me:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BlazorWebAssemblyEnableLinking>true</BlazorWebAssemblyEnableLinking>
  <MonoLinkerI18NAssemblies>all</MonoLinkerI18NAssemblies>
</PropertyGroup>
```

See also https://github.com/dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs/issues/15679

comments: Thanks @catlan ... stand-by ... these issues are usually triaged on Fridays.

Thanks for contacting us, @catlan.
That setting is actually used only by the linker. When linker is disabled, the effect is similar as having the setting set to `all` for linker-enabled scenario.
Is this not what you're observing?

No, what I'm observing is similar as having the setting set to `none`. 

Is there any debug information I can provide?
We will need a repro project, unless you experience this with a newly created project.

review_comments: Nit: I would change this function name to reflect the fact that the behavior is a little different without the linker enabled (e.g. assemblies that are not set in `BlazorWebAssemblyI18NAssemblies` are not copied.

We already verify that the test does not copy additional assemblies when you have the linker enabled. The fact that we include additional assemblies when it isn't is an implementation defect, I don't think we need to document it as part of the test name. We could very well improve it in the future if we get feedback.
